pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented as four days a week, the most efficient way to train, first month devoted to form at a weight 'light enough that if you do it wrong, you won't get hurt', with mobility framed as joints, tendons, ligaments and fascia so 'you don't want to get injured. We don't need to have chronic pains. We want you to be able to run around with the kids.' He agreed without pushback and asked only logistics questions about the bell itself — 'should I have one or two of those?'. He had already pre-sold himself on the modality: 'I like the idea of just doing kind of natural movements and just building up all the muscles rather than just targeting specific muscle groups... I just want to be able to move however I want to and not hurt.'

Presented as eating for health rather than restriction, with weight loss as a side effect. He engaged by surfacing the constraint that has killed diets for him before — family friction: 'oh, David needs to eat keto, David needs to eat gluten-free or whatever. And the kids are over here eating chicken nuggets, and she's eating the same thing she's giving the kids. It's always just difficult.' Not pushback on the pillar, but a real condition on it. The rep answered well ('a lot of people put themselves on this big restriction like keto or going vegan or carnivore, it's not sustainable long term') and the prospect accepted.

The pillar that sold him, and he had already named it as his top need before it was presented: 'First would be just accountability. Not necessarily hey, get up, go do it. But like, hey, did you go do it? Sort of thing.' After the presentation he tied it straight back to himself: 'I like the idea of me just kind of doing my thing with someone checking in, and if I need help, I can ask for it. And someone just making sure, hey, you're doing what you're supposed to do. That sounds like the best of all the worlds.' He also endorsed the education framing against his own professional values: 'I definitely want to learn. I don't just want to monkey see, monkey do. That's part of my job is making sure people are trained up.'

anchors.raw: given we've had a lot of money discussions over the last several months, and I'm like, hey, we're spending too much, got to tail back... it's like the money's just going out the door, no matter how much I make, it's all gone
anchors.note: The decisive anchor. It is not a competitor price but an active household austerity policy that the prospect himself instituted, which makes a $6,000 personal discretionary purchase politically expensive at home regardless of value. Compounded by a stated joint-decision rule on anything over three figures. The rep acknowledged it in one word and never explored it, so no payment plan, deposit or staged start was offered against the one obstacle that actually decides this deal.

anchors.raw: I've been watching the videos, whatever his name is. There's like little five-minute morning routine. And there's like, I've been going through them and like, there's one exercise, I'm like, I don't really know what it's supposed to be
anchors.competitor: Trevor's own free social media content
anchors.note: He is already following Primal's free mobility routines and getting some benefit, which sets the baseline the paid product must beat. The rep did not convert it — the honest admission that he cannot tell whether he is doing the McGregors correctly is the single sharpest argument for paid coaching on the call, and it was answered with 'Yeah, I've got you on' rather than developed.

The prospect immediately converted the price to a monthly figure and the rep followed him into it, confirming '$7.50' per month for the twelve. That reframes a coaching engagement as a recurring subscription and invites comparison against gym memberships and apps rather than against outcomes. He has a history of buying memberships he does not use, which makes that comparison actively unhelpful.

anchors.raw: I started doing calisthenics and just like doing like, just as simple as like, just do 10 pushups, 10 sit, 10 squats. I do that like once a day. And then I went up doing that like three times a day. And just added more and more here and there.
anchors.note: He has already engineered a large recovery — from unable to stand at a sink to running around the backyard — with free bodyweight work and no coach. The rep congratulated it repeatedly ('You've come a long way, man. You should be proud of yourself') without ever reframing why the next six points on his 10-point scale need something the first four did not.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that loaded kettlebell training is appropriate for a body with a possible ankylosing spondylitis diagnosis and recurring knee flare-ups
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There is no screening or clearance step anywhere in the process. The programme's answer was to defer the entire question until after purchase — 'let us know all of the past with it in terms of the joint pain, in terms of the chronic, all of that, let us know, be detailed about it when you're on with Trevor' — while simultaneously guaranteeing a progression to a 55 lb bell on every movement. The prospect never got an answer to whether he is a safe candidate, because nothing in the offer produces one before payment.

unmet_demand.want: A nutrition plan that does not require him to eat differently from his wife and children
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Genuinely served — the programme's whole positioning is sustainability over restriction, and the rep said so. But the answer stayed general and never became concrete about how one household eats one dinner. Given that family friction is what killed both his previous dietary attempts, this needed a specific example and did not get one.

unmet_demand.want: A way to buy this without a lump sum, given income without liquidity and an active household spending freeze
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No payment plan was offered or mentioned on this call, even though instalments were structured live for another prospect the previous day. The prospect disclosed the exact conditions instalments exist for and was quoted a single lump figure.

unmet_demand.want: To be able to start immediately — he has no kettlebell and two failed deliveries
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Handled well and closed out: 'Your first day is on your first workout day. So it's not like, oh, my kettlebell hasn't arrived, I've lost a month.' Recorded because it is a recurring friction in a home-equipment-dependent programme and the fix appears to be improvised per call rather than a stated policy.
